Build & Deploy Static Sites with Julia

BonitoSites is a powerful toolkit for creating and deploying static websites built with Bonito.jl. Generate documentation sites, blogs, and web content with built-in deployment to GitHub Pages.

Key Features

Easy Deployment

Deploy your Bonito applications to GitHub Pages with a single function call. Automatic handling of branch management and push operations.

Markdown Blog Support

Create blogs from Markdown files with automatic RSS feed generation. Perfect for documentation sites and technical blogs.

Malt-Based Processing

Run code in isolated Julia processes using Malt.jl for safe and reproducible content generation.

Rich Components

Built-in components for code highlighting, video embedding, and social media integration.

RSS Feed Generation

Automatically generate RSS feeds from your site entries for easy content syndication.

GitHub Integration

Seamless integration with GitHub for repository information and automated workflows.

Installation

Install BonitoSites directly from GitHub:

                  using Pkg
Pkg.add(url="https://github.com/SimonDanisch/BonitoSites.jl")

Quick Start

Get started with BonitoSites in just a few lines of code:

                  using Bonito
using BonitoSites

# Create a simple app
app = App() do
    DOM.div(
        DOM.h1("Hello, World!"),
        DOM.p("My first Bonito site")
    )
end

# Create routes
routes = Routes("/" => app)

# Export as static site
Bonito.export_static("build", routes)

# Deploy to GitHub Pages
BonitoSites.deploy(
    "github.com/yourusername/yourrepo.git";
    push_preview=true,
    devbranch="main",
    devurl="docs"
)

Use Cases

  • Documentation Sites: Generate beautiful documentation from Bonito applications with automatic deployment.
  • Technical Blogs: Create markdown-based blogs with RSS feeds and code execution.
  • Project Showcases: Build interactive demonstrations of your Julia projects.
  • Static Web Apps: Deploy any Bonito application as a static website.
